gaps.sentence: 'I might take a gap year,' he said. He said he ___ take a gap year.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form; it stays might.

gaps.sentence: "I am sorry I am late." — He ___ for being late.
gaps.explanation: 'Apologise for doing something' reports an apology.
Apologise for + -ing; the other verbs do not take 'for + -ing' in this pattern.

gaps.sentence: She ___ on seeing the manager immediately.
gaps.explanation: Only 'insist' takes on + -ing; suggest and offer take bare -ing/to-infinitive respectively.

gaps.sentence: 'No, I won't open the door,' he said. He ___ to open the door.
gaps.explanation: Refusals are reported with refuse + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'Which seat do you prefer?' the steward asked. The steward asked which seat I ___.
gaps.explanation: do you prefer → I preferred: statement order, present simple backshifted.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm exhausted,' she said. She said she ___ exhausted.
gaps.explanation: Present simple/progressive shifts to past in reported speech: am → was.

gaps.sentence: 'Will you marry me?' he asked her. He asked her ___ marry him.
gaps.explanation: Will you...? → if/whether she would...: statement word order, backshifted modal.
